comments.author: fogzen
comments.why: Datafun author explains a total functional Datalog generalization
comments.text: Yes, for some kinds of operations on some kinds of data structures. The keyword/property is "monotonicity". Monotonic functions are guaranteed to terminate under fixed-point semantics. Look into Datafun: A total functional language that generalizes Datalog. Also be sure to watch Datafun author Michael Arntzenius's Strangeloop talk. [LINK] [VIDEO]

comments.author: tracnar
comments.story: Why Can't Database Tables Index Themselves? (2006)
comments.why: Talk explores SQL-like language with automatic indexing
comments.text: This talk explored a bit that idea, you could have a (full) programming language which is more like SQL so you get good enough datastructures (and indexing- without manual tuning: [VIDEO] I think Prolog (another commenter pointed it out) and datalog do this to some extend.
